server_arguments.name: trust_remote_code
server_arguments.label: trust-remote-code
server_arguments.desc: Whether you want to execute hub modelling code. Explicitly passing a `revision` is encouraged when loading a model with custom code to ensure no malicious code has been contributed in a newer revision

server_arguments.name: dtype
server_arguments.label: dtype
server_arguments.desc: The dtype to be forced upon the model. This option cannot be used with `--quantize`

server_arguments.name: kv_cache_dtype
server_arguments.label: kv-cache-dtype
server_arguments.desc: Specify the dtype for the key-value cache. When this option is not provided, the dtype of the model is used (typically `float16` or `bfloat16`). Currently the only supported value are `fp8_e4m3fn` and `fp8_e5m2` on CUDA

server_arguments.name: quantize
server_arguments.label: quantize
server_arguments.desc: Quantization method to use for the model. It is not necessary to specify this option for pre-quantized models, since the quantization method is read from the model configuration

server_arguments.name: max_concurrent_requests
server_arguments.label: max-concurrent-requests
server_arguments.desc: The maximum amount of concurrent requests for this particular deployment. Having a low limit will refuse clients requests instead of having them wait for too long and is usually good to handle backpressure correctly

server_arguments.name: max_input_tokens
server_arguments.label: max-input-tokens
server_arguments.desc: This is the maximum allowed input length (expressed in number of tokens) for users. The larger this value, the longer prompt users can send which can impact the overall memory required to handle the load. Please note that some models have a finite range of sequence they can handle. Default to min(max_allocatable, max_position_embeddings) - 1

server_arguments.name: max_total_tokens
server_arguments.label: max-total-tokens
server_arguments.desc: This is the most important value to set as it defines the 'memory budget' of running clients requests. Clients will send input sequences and ask to generate `max_new_tokens` on top. with a value of `1512` users can send either a prompt of `1000` and ask for `512` new tokens, or send a prompt of `1` and ask for `1511` max_new_tokens. The larger this value, the larger amount each request will be in your RAM and the less effective batching can be. Default to min(max_allocatable, max_position_embeddings)

server_arguments.name: max_batch_prefill_tokens
server_arguments.label: max-batch-prefill-tokens
server_arguments.desc: Limits the number of tokens for the prefill operation. Since this operation take the most memory and is compute bound, it is interesting to limit the number of requests that can be sent. Default to `max_input_tokens + 50` to give a bit of room

server_arguments.name: max_batch_total_tokens
server_arguments.label: max-batch-total-tokens
server_arguments.desc:
**IMPORTANT** This is one critical control to allow maximum usage of the available hardware. 
This represents the total amount of potential tokens within a batch. When using padding (not recommended) this would be equivalent of `batch_size` * `max_total_tokens`. 
However in the non-padded (flash attention) version this can be much finer. 
For `max_batch_total_tokens=1000`, you could fit `10` queries of `total_tokens=100` or a single query of `1000` tokens. 
Overall this number should be the largest possible amount that fits the remaining memory (after the model is loaded). Since the actual memory overhead depends on other parameters like if you're using quantization, flash attention or the model implementation, text-generation-inference cannot infer this number automatically.

server_arguments.name: max_waiting_tokens
server_arguments.label: max-waiting-tokens
server_arguments.desc: This setting defines how many tokens can be passed before forcing the waiting queries to be put on the batch (if the size of the batch allows for it). New queries require 1 `prefill` forward, which is different from `decode` and therefore you need to pause the running batch in order to run `prefill` to create the correct values for the waiting queries to be able to join the batch.

server_arguments.name: max_batch_size
server_arguments.label: max-batch-size
server_arguments.desc: Enforce a maximum number of requests per batch Specific flag for hardware targets that do not support unpadded inference

server_arguments.name: max_client_batch_size
server_arguments.label: max-client-batch-size
server_arguments.desc: Control the maximum number of inputs that a client can send in a single request

server_arguments.name: enable_prefill_logprobs
server_arguments.label: enable-prefill-logprobs
server_arguments.desc: Logprobs in the prompt are deactivated by default because they consume a large amount of VRAM (especially for long prompts). Using this flag reallows users to ask for them

server_arguments.name: cuda_graphs
server_arguments.label: cuda-graphs
server_arguments.desc: Specify the batch sizes to compute cuda graphs for. Use '0' to disable

server_arguments.name: rope_scaling
server_arguments.label: rope-scaling
server_arguments.desc:
Rope scaling will only be used for RoPE models and allow rescaling the position rotary to accomodate for larger prompts. 
Goes together with `rope_factor`. 
`--rope-factor 2.0` gives linear scaling with a factor of 2.0 `--rope-scaling dynamic` gives dynamic scaling with a factor of 1.0 `--rope-scaling linear` gives linear scaling with a factor of 1.0 (Nothing will be changed basically) 
`--rope-scaling linear --rope-factor` fully describes the scaling you want

server_arguments.name: rope_factor
server_arguments.label: rope-factor
server_arguments.desc: Rope scaling will only be used for RoPE models See `rope_scaling`

server_arguments.name: waiting_served_ratio
server_arguments.label: waiting-served-ratio
server_arguments.desc:
This represents the ratio of waiting queries vs running queries where you want to start considering pausing the running queries to include the waiting ones into the same batch. `waiting_served_ratio=1.2` Means when 12 queries are waiting and there's only 10 queries left in the current batch we check if we can fit those 12 waiting queries into the batching strategy, and if yes, then batching happens delaying the 10 running queries by a `prefill` run. 
This setting is only applied if there is room in the batch as defined by `max_batch_total_tokens`.

server_arguments.name: max_best_of
server_arguments.label: max-best-of
server_arguments.desc: This is the maximum allowed value for clients to set `best_of`. Best of makes `n` generations at the same time, and return the best in terms of overall log probability over the entire generated sequence

server_arguments.name: max_stop_sequences
server_arguments.label: max-stop-sequences
server_arguments.desc: This is the maximum allowed value for clients to set `stop_sequences`. Stop sequences are used to allow the model to stop on more than just the EOS token, and enable more complex 'prompting' where users can preprompt the model in a specific way and define their 'own' stop token aligned with their prompt

server_arguments.name: max_top_n_tokens
server_arguments.label: max-top-n-tokens
server_arguments.desc: This is the maximum allowed value for clients to set `top_n_tokens`. `top_n_tokens` is used to return information about the the `n` most likely tokens at each generation step, instead of just the sampled token. This information can be used for downstream tasks like for classification or ranking

server_arguments.name: validation_workers
server_arguments.label: validation-workers
server_arguments.desc: The number of tokenizer workers used for payload validation and truncation inside the router

server_arguments.name: disable_custom_kernels
server_arguments.label: disable-custom-kernels
server_arguments.desc: For some models (like bloom), text-generation-inference implemented custom cuda kernels to speed up inference. Those kernels were only tested on A100. Use this flag to disable them if you're running on different hardware and encounter issues

server_arguments.name: cuda_memory_fraction
server_arguments.label: cuda-memory-fraction
server_arguments.desc: Limit the CUDA available memory. The allowed value equals the total visible memory multiplied by cuda-memory-fraction

server_arguments.name: disable_grammar_support
server_arguments.label: disable-grammar-support
server_arguments.desc: Disable outlines grammar constrained generation. This is a feature that allows you to generate text that follows a specific grammar

arguments.name: temperature
arguments.label: temperature
arguments.desc: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic

arguments.name: top_p
arguments.label: top_p
arguments.desc: An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered

arguments.name: top_k
arguments.label: top_k
arguments.desc: The number of highest probability vocabulary tokens to keep for top-k-filtering

arguments.name: max_tokens
arguments.label: max_tokens
arguments.desc: The maximum number of tokens to generate in the chat completion

arguments.name: min_tokens
arguments.label: min_tokens
arguments.desc: The minimum number of tokens to generate in the chat completion

arguments.name: stop
arguments.label: stop_sequences
arguments.desc: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens

arguments.name: presence_penalty
arguments.label: presence_penalty
arguments.desc: Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics

arguments.name: frequency_penalty
arguments.label: frequency_penalty
arguments.desc: Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far, decreasing the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim

arguments.name: logit_bias
arguments.label: logit_bias
arguments.desc: Accepts a json object that maps tokens (specified by their token ID in the tokenizer) to an associated bias value from -100 to 100. Mathematically, the bias is added to the logits generated by the model prior to sampling

arguments.name: ignore_eos
arguments.label: ignore_eos
arguments.desc: Whether to ignore the EOS token and continue generating tokens after the EOS token is generated.

arguments.name: use_beam_search
arguments.label: use_beam_search
arguments.desc: Whether to use beam search instead of sampling.

arguments.name: stop_token_ids
arguments.label: stop_token_ids
arguments.desc: List of tokens that stop the generation when they are generated. The returned output will contain the stop tokens unless the stop tokens are special tokens.

arguments.name: skip_special_tokens
arguments.label: skip_special_tokens
arguments.desc: Whether to skip special tokens in the output.
